name: Nandrolone

lead: Nandrolone is an injectable anabolic steroid, best known as nandrolone decanoate (Deca-Durabolin). It has been prescribed for wasting, anaemia of kidney disease and osteoporosis, and bodybuilders use it for a bigger, fuller physique, with users also citing joint comfort and, in looksmax posts, hair-friendliness and bone growth.

It activates the androgen receptor and, unlike testosterone, is converted to a weaker androgen (DHN) rather than DHT; it also has progestogenic activity. Clinical trials in patients have examined lean mass, bone and blood outcomes and show effects on lean mass. No controlled trial in healthy people for appearance was found, and the bone-growth claim is untested.

paras: Lifters generally use it in cycles with heavy training, commonly alongside testosterone, since it suppresses natural production. Supply for non-medical use is illicit, and a systematic review describes illicit use as widespread among adolescents and bodybuilders.

Reviews of illicit use report adverse effects across several organ systems, and cardiac deaths have been reported in anabolic steroid users generally. It suppresses natural testosterone production, is a US Schedule III drug, and is prohibited in sport.

chain: Greater lean mass and joint comfort
angle.text: Nandrolone (Deca) is an injectable steroid used by lifters for muscle size and, per forum claims, joint comfort and bone growth, through anabolic signalling in muscle. Trials show lean-mass gains in patients with illness, and none exist in healthy lifters.

lead: Nandrolone, also called 19-nortestosterone, is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) derived from testosterone by removal of one methyl group, and it is the parent compound of the 19-nor AAS subclass.[1][2] It is usually given as an injectable ester, most often nandrolone decanoate (brand name Deca-Durabolin) or the shorter-acting nandrolone phenylpropionate (Durabolin).[2] Wikipedia describes it as among the most widely used anabolic steroids worldwide.[2]

People use nandrolone to look more muscular. Bodybuilders and other physique athletes use it, usually at doses above medical ones, for muscle size, strength and joint and recovery benefits, and the chain proponents describe runs from more training capacity and recovery to more muscle mass.[1][3] Looksmaxxing forum users also discuss it because of its pharmacology: it is converted to a weaker androgen in skin and scalp rather than amplified, which is the basis of claims that it is gentler on hair than testosterone.[2]

Medically, nandrolone esters have been used for catabolic and wasting conditions, anaemia of chronic kidney disease, osteoporosis and burns, although this use has become increasingly rare.[2] Trials have been run in patients, and a 2020 systematic review of 148 papers catalogued the adverse effects reported in illicit users.[3] No controlled trial in healthy people for physique purposes has been published. Nandrolone is a controlled substance in many countries and is prohibited in sport.[2]
infobox: US Schedule III; UK Class C; Canada Schedule IV; prohibited in sport[2]

paras: Nandrolone esters have been indicated for anaemia associated with chronic kidney disease, postmenopausal osteoporosis, and wasting in HIV/AIDS, burns and cancer, where they stimulate red blood cell production, appetite and lean mass.[1][2] Medical doses are described as far lower than those used illicitly.[1]

Wikipedia notes that clinical use is now increasingly rare and that nandrolone sulfate has been used in an eye drop for corneal healing.[2] Its high ratio of anabolic to androgenic activity is why 19-nor steroids became the most frequently used anabolic steroids in clinical settings where anabolic effects are wanted, such as AIDS cachexia, severe burns and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.[2]

Competitive athletes, bodybuilders and powerlifters use nandrolone esters for physique and performance.[2] Non-medical users describe it as a muscle-building and joint- and recovery-supporting compound, often stacked with testosterone.[1][3] A systematic review of illicit nandrolone decanoate use describes the drug class as widespread among adolescents and bodybuilders because of its anabolic properties and its capacity to raise exercise tolerance.[3]
On looksmax.org, users discuss deca as a muscle compound said not to cause hair loss, and some argue it may support bone density or growth. These are community claims; see the claims section below.

Nandrolone is an agonist of the androgen receptor (AR), the target of testosterone and dihydrotestosterone (DHT).[2] Unlike testosterone, it is not potentiated in androgenic tissues such as scalp, skin and prostate: 5-alpha-reductase converts it to 5-alpha-dihydronandrolone (DHN), a weaker AR ligand, so it is attenuated rather than amplified there.[2] Wikipedia accordingly describes its anabolic-to-androgenic ratio as very high; rodent figures quoted range from roughly 1:3 to 1:16, and Grokipedia gives about 11:1.[1][2] This is the pharmacological basis of forum claims that deca is 'hair safe', although Wikipedia says scalp hair loss is possible but theoretical.[2]

Nandrolone is also a potent progestogen, binding the progesterone receptor with about 22 percent of the affinity of progesterone, which augments its antigonadotropic (testosterone-suppressing) effect.[2] Because it is not 17-alpha-alkylated, its hepatotoxic potential is described as much lower than oral steroids, and its reduced interaction with aromatase lessens estrogenic effects, although gynecomastia and reduced libido can still occur at high doses.[2]

Oral bioavailability is very low, so it is given as injectable esters.[2] Esterification at the 17-beta hydroxyl creates oil-soluble depots; the elimination half-life of the decanoate after intramuscular injection is listed as 6-12 days, and a single injection of decanoate produces an anabolic effect for roughly 20-25 days compared with 10-14 days for phenylpropionate.[2] Nandrolone binds sex hormone-binding globulin weakly, about 5 percent as strongly as testosterone.[2] Its urinary metabolites include 19-norandrosterone and 19-noretiocholanolone, which anti-doping labs measure.[2]

Nandrolone (C18H26O2, molar mass about 274 g/mol) is the C19-demethylated analogue of testosterone and occurs naturally in trace amounts as an intermediate in estradiol biosynthesis.[2] It is the parent compound of a group of anabolic steroids that includes trenbolone, and of the norethisterone family of progestins.[2][4] It is made semi-synthetically by Birch reduction of an estrogen precursor, a route first described in 1953; decanoate is made by treating nandrolone with decanoic anhydride.[1][2]

Wikipedia reports that nandrolone was first synthesised in 1950 and introduced as nandrolone phenylpropionate (Durabolin) in 1959 and as nandrolone decanoate (Deca-Durabolin) in 1962, followed by other esters.[2] The Birch reduction route to the 19-nor steroid skeleton had been described in 1953.[1]

It was probably among the first anabolic steroids used for doping in sport in the 1960s and has been banned at the Olympics since 1974.[2] A 1981 randomised comparative trial published in the New England Journal of Medicine compared androgens for anaemia in patients on haemodialysis, part of the clinical literature that made nandrolone esters a standard anabolic agent in nephrology.[5] Osteoporosis was intensively studied; esters increased calcium uptake and reduced bone loss, but virilisation was reported in about half of women and use declined once bisphosphonates became available.[2]

Trials have tested nandrolone decanoate in patients rather than healthy lifters. A randomised trial examined it in burned patients, with the authors suggesting a new indication after its recall;[6] a randomised trial in men with osteoporosis examined bone outcomes;[7] a 1981 randomised comparison studied androgens for anaemia in haemodialysis patients;[5] and a double-blind pilot randomised 20 women with primary Sjogren's syndrome to nandrolone decanoate or placebo for six months, reporting moderate improvement in dry mouth symptoms and a drop in erythrocyte sedimentation rate.[8] A phase 1/2 study of 20 people with telomere-related bone marrow failure and lung disease has been completed,[9] with an editorial in Haematologica discussing nandrolone as a possible option for telomeropathies.[10]

Registered studies have also covered HIV-associated weight loss in women (38 participants),[11] cancer cachexia (60 participants),[12] and muscle loss with leucine (30 participants).[13] A forum poster cites a study in dialysis patients reporting that 6 months of weekly nandrolone raised lean body mass, offered as evidence for the compound. No trial of nandrolone for cosmetic or bodybuilding purposes in healthy people has been published.

A 2020 systematic review of 148 eligible papers (from 766 screened) on nandrolone decanoate abuse and adverse effects summarised the most frequent effects in abusers, with the reproductive and other organ systems affected.[3] A separate review of sudden cardiac death in AAS users examined cardiac mechanisms in 33 reported cases across the drug class.[14] A review of the related steroid trenbolone, a nandrolone derivative, reports that severe acne and gynecomastia affect roughly a third of its users and describes injection-site complications with contaminated products; those figures concern trenbolone, not nandrolone itself.[4]

Wikipedia lists acne, facial and body hair growth, voice changes and clitoral enlargement as possible effects in women, cardiovascular toxicity, hypogonadism and infertility at high doses, and notes scalp hair loss as possible but theoretical, consistent with the metabolite DHN being a much weaker AR ligand.[2] Users on looksmax.org note that both testosterone and deca suppress natural testosterone production, and one thread is titled as a complaint that deca caused insulin resistance.

Nandrolone is a Schedule III controlled substance in the United States, Class C in the UK, Schedule IV in Canada and Class C5 in Brazil, so non-medical use is generally illicit.[2] T Nation posters note that prescriptions for supraphysiological doses of testosterone, nandrolone and related drugs are a legal grey area.[15]

Nandrolone use is detected indirectly in urine through 19-norandrosterone; the IOC set a limit of 2.0 micrograms per litre, and a study of 621 athletes at the 1998 Nagano Olympics found none above 0.4.[2] Contaminated androstenedione supplements, sold over the counter in the US until 2004, were a known source of trace 19-norandrosterone.[2] Anti-doping analysis combines GC-MS with isotope ratio mass spectrometry to detect nandrolone and testosterone administration.[16]

Several high-profile athletes, including Merlene Ottey, Dieter Baumann and Linford Christie, were reported in 1999 cases; Wikipedia says the detection method was later shown to be faulty after Mark Richardson demonstrated a false positive in 2000.[2] C. J. Hunter initially blamed lysine supplements and told a grand jury in 2004 that he had injected nandrolone, and Marion Jones admitted steroid use in October 2007.[2]

On looksmax.org, deca is promoted by some as a muscle, skin and bone compound and dismissed by others as unnecessary alongside other drugs. Posts frame it within physique-building as a way to add muscle while avoiding the scalp effects associated with DHT-converting steroids. T Nation threads treat it as part of the broader steroid conversation in lifting culture.[15]

claims.claim: Deca is 'hair safe' because it converts to a weak androgen.
Deca builds a lot of muscle, as shown by trials.
Some users consider deca unnecessary alongside testosterone and HGH.
Deca is gentler on skin and hair than testosterone.
Deca is a joint-friendly recovery drug.
A prescription makes supraphysiological nandrolone legal.
